answer: Hardware remote attestation resists Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to bind its key in a trusted enclave and present a vendor-signed quote with a chip-bound ID. Because an attacker cannot mirror a sealed key across VMs, each fake identity demands scarce dedicated silicon, keeping clones from spreading like a vine. Far from an ivory tower theory, this check grounds trust in physical hardware, though side-channel leaks or compromised vendor keys can still enable forged quotes.
